claims.text: The baseline is a standard PVD-deposited, oxide-free FeNiCrCoCu HEA coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Introducing a minor reactive oxygen partial pressure during PVD can produce 2–5 vol% nano-oxide particles in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The resulting nano-oxide particles will be uniformly dispersed within the HEA matrix.
The nano-oxide particles will act as pinning centers for dislocations.
The nano-oxide particles will restrict grain-boundary motion.
Inhibition of dislocation motion and grain-boundary motion will reduce localized plastic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
Inhibition of dislocation motion and grain-boundary motion will reduce wear during high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the baseline, the nano-oxide-dispersed coating will exhibit lower wear volume at 550–650°C.
Relative to the baseline, the nano-oxide-dispersed coating will exhibit a reduced coefficient of friction at 550–650°C.
Relative to the baseline, the nano-oxide-dispersed coating will exhibit diminished localized deformation features at 550–650°C.
The predictions are expected to hold during sliding at 550–650°C under otherwise identical load, speed, and kinematics.
Departures from the controlled oxygen process window may prevent the expected improvements.
Tests outside 550–650°C may not produce the expected improvements.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in wear volume, friction, and localized deformation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that a lack of the improvements would falsify the hypothesis, which can imply failure of any predicted improvement, whereas the formal rule is conjunctive and appears to require failure to reduce wear, friction, and deformation together. This creates ambiguity about whether failure of only one outcome is decisive.
